paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jesus has just gone up to heaven, and the apostles are left with an empty spot in their group and no instructions for filling it. So what do they do first? They go to the upper room and "with one accord they all continued in prayer" (Acts 1:14). Before they make a single plan, they talk to God.

Now look at how they handle the choice. Peter points to the Scripture, and it says "May another take his position" (Acts 1:20). They set out what the job needs: someone who has been there the whole time and can be a witness of the resurrection (Acts 1:21-22). Then they pray, "Lord, You know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen" (Acts 1:24). Notice what they ask. They don't ask God to bless their pick. They ask Him to show them His.

Here's the lesson for you, baker. When a big decision lands on you, you can do what they did: pray first, listen to what God has already said, then ask Him to show you what He has chosen. They knew the decision was His to make, and that's a relief, because you don't have to guess alone. I once spent years in a dark drawer thinking nobody was choosing anything for me, and I was WRONG. God's plans don't wait on us to figure them out. And Judas leaving a hole didn't leave God's work with one.
